title: Sell Mineral Rights in Plentywood, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Plentywood, MT
metaDescription: Plentywood is Sheridan County's seat, on the thinner edge of the Bakken. I buy mineral interests here, priced against real production, not ND-core hype.
heroLead: Plentywood is the courthouse town for the whole county, and it's also where I start every title search on a Sheridan County interest, no matter which small town the family calls from.
intro: Of everywhere in Sheridan County, Plentywood has seen the most consistent Bakken-era activity, closer to the play's stronger extension than the ground further west toward the Saskatchewan line. That said, I want to be straight with anyone calling from here: consistent activity in an edge county still means thinner net pay and lower well density than the North Dakota core, and the royalty checks reflect that difference. I evaluate your interest against its actual production record, not against what the county courthouse gossip says about the boom years.
Being the county seat also means Plentywood is where every other town's title work eventually routes through, so I know this record about as well as any in the county.

sections.heading: What I check first for a Plentywood-area interest
paragraphs: I pull the recorded chain from the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder right here in town, confirm whether the interest is currently leased or unleased, and check nearby well production and decline. Plentywood-area interests are more likely than most in the county to have an active lease on file, but that doesn't mean every parcel does.

sections.heading: Older conventional layers under the newer leases
paragraphs: This county had conventional Madison-formation production decades before the Bakken boom, and some of that older leasing history still shows up in the record around Plentywood. I check for both eras rather than assuming your family's interest is purely a Bakken-era story.

faqs.question: Is Plentywood the most active part of Sheridan County?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, relative to the rest of the county, though still on the thinner western edge of the Bakken compared to North Dakota core acreage.

faqs.question: Where do you pull the deed records for Plentywood-area interests?
faqs.answer: Directly from the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder here in town — I don't ask you to track it down.

faqs.question: Could my family's old lease be from before the Bakken boom?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if it traces to the 1950s or 60s conventional Madison production era. I check the full record before quoting.

faqs.question: Why does being the county seat matter for my title search?
faqs.answer: It doesn't change your parcel's value, but it does mean I'm already deeply familiar with the record system I'll be pulling your documents from.
